styles.name: Dravidian Style
styles.primaryRegion: South India (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala)
styles.primaryMaterials: Granite, Charnockite, Sandstone, Lost-wax cast Bronze
coreFeatures: Stepped pyramidal sanctum tower known as the Vimana
Towering monumental entrance gateway towers known as Gopurams
Compound enclosure wall (Prakara) with cloistered pillared corridors
Octagonal or domical crowning cupola (Shikhara / Stupika) surmounted by a single Kalasha finial
Enclosed pillared assembly halls (Mandapa, Ardhamandapa, Mahamandapa)
styles.sculpturalHallmarks: Dynamic movement in relief, monumental guardian Dvarapalas with crossed clubs, serene bronze processional deities (Utsava Murtis), and extensive epigraphic friezes along the plinth (Adhisthana).
canonicalMonuments: Shore Temple & Pancha Rathas, Mamallapuram (Tamil Nadu)
styles.dynasticDistinction: Dravidian represents an overarching architectural taxonomic category defined in the Manasara and Mayamata treatises. It was championed successively by the Pallava, Chola, Pandya, Vijayanagara, and Nayaka dynasties, each introducing distinct innovations (e.g., Pallavas introduced monolithic rock-cut forms; Cholas perfected soaring Vimanas; Nayakas expanded multi-acre corridors and massive Gopurams).

styles.name: Nagara Style
styles.primaryRegion: North & Central India (Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh)
styles.primaryMaterials: Buff Sandstone, Red Sandstone, White Marble, Granite
coreFeatures: Beehive-shaped curvilinear sanctuary tower (Shikhara) curving gently inward towards the summit
Large fluted circular stone disk crowning the spire called the Amalaka
Crowning water pitcher finial (Kalasha) atop the Amalaka
Elevated plinth platform (Jagati) accessed via grand stone stairs
Cruciform ground plan with projection bays (Rathas: Triratha, Pancharatha, Saptaratha)
styles.sculpturalHallmarks: High sensuality and organic plasticity; cascading vertical bands of celestial Surasundaris, Dikpalas, and auspicious Mithuna figures celebrating worldly abundance and divine bliss.
styles.dynasticDistinction: Nagara refers to the northern architectural order. Dynasties like the Guptas (classical originators), Gurjara-Pratiharas, Chandelas, Paramaras, and Solankis formulated specialized sub-schools (e.g., Khajuraho Latina/Sekhari type, Solanki Maru-Gurjara style).

styles.name: Vesara (Hybrid) Style
styles.primaryRegion: Deccan Plateau (Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh)
coreFeatures: Deliberate fusion of northern Nagara curvilinear profile with southern Dravidian tier articulation
Semi-circular or apsidal ground plan tendencies (Gajaprishtha / elephant back) in early examples
Reduced height of individual tiers with increased ornamental density
Wide pillared open mantapas facilitating community assembly
styles.sculpturalHallmarks: Exceptional narrative density, vigorous anatomical modeling, expressive animal friezes, and richly articulated ceiling rosettes.
canonicalMonuments: Durga Temple & Lad Khan Temple, Aihole (Karnataka)
styles.dynasticDistinction: Originating in the Malaprabha river valley under the Early Western Chalukyas of Badami, Vesara was further developed by the Rashtrakutas, Later Western Chalukyas of Kalyani, and Kakatiyas.

styles.name: Hoysala Style
styles.primaryMaterials: Chlorite Schist (Soft Soapstone that hardens over time)
coreFeatures: Stellate (star-shaped) ground plan with multiple projecting points creating immense exterior surface area
Raised wide circumambulatory terrace (Jagati) without an enclosing compound wall
Multiple shrines joined to a common central navaranga hall (Ekokata, Dvikuta, Trikuta)
Horizontal plinth friezes arranged in strict canonical order: Elephants (stability), Lions (courage), Horses (speed), Floral scrolls (beauty), and Epic narratives
styles.sculpturalHallmarks: Unrivalled micro-carving, deep undercutting where stone beads and ornaments can be freely touched behind figures, bracket maidens (Madanikas), and signed sculptor colophons.
styles.dynasticDistinction: Unique to the Hoysala realm. Enabled by the unique geological properties of chlorite schist and an imperial ethos that celebrated individual artisan identity.

styles.name: Kalinga Style
styles.primaryRegion: Odisha and Northern Andhra Coastal Belt
coreFeatures: Deula architectural taxonomy: Rekha Deula (tall sanctum tower with curvilinear shikhara)
Pidhi Deula / Jagamohana (stepped pyramidal assembly hall for devotees)
Khakhara Deula (semi-cylindrical barrel-vaulted sanctum dedicated exclusively to Shakta goddesses)
Absence of interior pillars in monumental halls, relying on corbelled stone vaulting and iron beams
styles.sculpturalHallmarks: Heavy, voluptuous feminine forms playing musical instruments, Alasa Kanyas (indolent maidens), colossal guardian animals, and astronomical wheel carvings.
styles.dynasticDistinction: Patronized by the Sailodbhava, Bhauma-Kara, Somavamsi, and Eastern Ganga dynasties over eight centuries of continuous architectural evolution.

styles.name: Pallava Tradition
coreFeatures: Four chronological evolutionary phases: Mahendra style (rock-cut pillared caves), Mamalla style (monolithic Rathas & open-air reliefs), Rajasimha style (early structural temples), Nandivarman style (small structural shrines)
Slender, lion-based pillar shafts (Simhavishnu columns) where rearing or seated lions support the capital
Kudu horseshoe-shaped arched dormer windows adorning cornices
styles.sculpturalHallmarks: Slender, graceful figures with elongated limbs, naturalistic non-rigid postures, restrained jewelry, and deep spiritual introspection.
canonicalMonuments: Arjuna's Penance & Pancha Rathas, Mamallapuram (Tamil Nadu)
styles.dynasticDistinction: A foundational dynastic school that transitioned South Indian sacred architecture from perishable timber and brick to permanent stone carving ('Vichitrachitta' / genius innovator Mahendravarman I).

styles.name: Chola Tradition
styles.primaryMaterials: Gneissoid Granite, Lost-wax cast Panchaloha Bronze
coreFeatures: Monumentalization of the Vimana tower, which dwarfed the entrance gopurams during the Imperial phase
Introduction of extensive royal inscriptions running along the base tiers detailing administration, arts, and endowments
Elaborate niche iconography (Devakoshtha) housing Ardhanarisvara, Dakshinamurti, Lingodbhava, and Durga
styles.sculpturalHallmarks: Incomparable bronze metallurgical mastery (cire-perdue); rhythmic balance between muscular vigor and yogic serenity; iconic dancing Natarajas.
styles.dynasticDistinction: The maritime Chola empire exported this aesthetic across the Indian Ocean to Sri Lanka, Sumatra, and the Khmer Empire of Cambodia.

styles.name: Vijayanagara Tradition
coreFeatures: Vast multi-columned ceremonial halls (Kalyana Mandapa, Ranga Mandapa) with hundreds of ornate pillars
Towering Raya Gopurams welcoming pilgrims from afar
Integration of civic, defensive, and sacred spaces inside immense urban fortified complexes
styles.sculpturalHallmarks: Rearing Yali and armed equestrian monoliths carved from solid granite pillars, musical SaReGaMa columns, stone chariots, and portrait sculptures of royal donors.
styles.dynasticDistinction: A pan-South Indian imperial resurgence that synthesized Kannada, Telugu, and Tamil artistic motifs to preserve and celebrate classical Indian heritage.
